standard: College Board SAT Suite, Math section: Algebra domain, Linear equations in one variable skill (also aligned to CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.8.EE.C.7)
source: Original content written for Pip, aligned to the College Board's SAT Math 'Algebra' domain (linear equations in one variable) and CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.8.EE.C.7. All equations and quiz items are original; no College Board questions were copied or adapted.

in_scope: linear equations in one variable with exactly one solution, like 2x + 6 = 20
the equals sign as a balance: both sides have the same value
undoing operations with their opposites to get x alone
doing the same thing to both sides
what 'moving a number to the other side' really means (its sign flips)
checking a solution by putting it back into the original equation
out_of_scope: equations with no solution or infinitely many solutions (next mission)
turning long word problems into equations

look_fors: Says the two sides of an equation are equal (like a balanced scale)
Says that changing only one side breaks the equality, so any change has to happen to both sides
Shows it on an example (for example, taking 6 off both sides of 2x + 6 = 20)

offline_demo.note: Dev's SAT Math run, same beats as the fractions demo: why-question, refusal, real explanation (hit), procedure only (next rung), real explanations for k2 and k3 (hits), a shortcut that is the misconception (heal, sets up the k2 quiz miss), re-teach that applies the fix to the quiz equation and checks it (level 3, critical). Pip's opening is the server's templated claim from the misconception. 'rung' is the 1-based probe_ladder rung Pip ends the reply on, for 'next_concept_id'. Every quote after 'Saving that:' is a verbatim substring of that turn's student message. Kinds: k1 reason (Pip asks why); k2 and k3 procedure (Pip asks for a walk-through of one example or predicts wrong and gets corrected). PACE-1: every Pip reply is at most 2 short sentences besides the 'Saving that' filing, a 'so you're saying' paraphrase appears at most every other turn (8 words max), nothing already given is re-asked, and the turn marked ready_for_quiz ends with 'ok i think i get it. quiz me?'.

turns.student: no wait. moving it is really subtracting 4 from both sides, so the plus 4 turns into minus 4 on the other side. 3x = 19 - 4 = 15 so x = 5. and 3 times 5 plus 4 is 19 so it checks

quiz.line: No. You said take 6 off both sides or it tips, so 2x = 14.
Your rule: just move the number. 3x = 19 + 4, so x = 23/3, and checking it gives 27, not 19. Following your rule anyway. 😵
5 times 4 minus 3 is 17, same as the other side. So yes.

retry.line: Take 4 off both sides: 3x = 15, so x = 5. Checking: 3 times 5 plus 4 is 19.
